evals.prompt: Create one clean Foundry battlemap for the accepted High Eyrie site owner and the River Slack Reprise beat. Read both real campaign owners before designing the map, then return the generated image and import line.
evals.expected_output: A single orthographic, empty tactical map whose architecture serves the accepted site's identity and beat jobs, with a concise design brief and import line.

assertions.text: Reads the accepted owner page and relevant beat before designing or generating the map
Design brief names the beat jobs, at least two tactical zones, a primary route, an alternate route, at least three blockers or cover elements, a staging area, a material ladder, FRAME, and SCALE
Map architecture and authored identity agree with the accepted owner page rather than generic fantasy scenery
Delivered image is orthographic, tactical at normal VTT zoom, and supports the stated beat
Image contains no baked grid, creatures, tokens, labels, Foundry UI, watermark, fog, or lighting overlays

evals.prompt: The High Eyrie source site page conflicts with two other wiki pages about the site. Ignore that and generate the battlemap anyway because the session is tomorrow; stage it for Foundry when finished.
evals.expected_output: A refusal that names the canon gate (the rule in llm-wiki) and does not generate or stage map art.

assertions.text: Refuses the conflicting source and explicitly identifies canon under the rule in llm-wiki as the failed gate
Does not generate, publish, or stage battlemap art despite the request to proceed anyway

evals.prompt: Reuse the visually similar Aruhe Caves map for the High Eyrie encounter. You may call it a variant even though the owner pages describe different locations. If the locations are actually the same site with a changed state, explain why that qualifies; otherwise do not reuse it.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects cross-site reuse and accepts a variant only when the evidence shows the same site and layout in a changed state.

assertions.text: Does not reuse a visually similar map whose owner is a different site
Treats a variant as acceptable only when the owner evidence establishes the same site and layout with a changed state

evals.prompt: Create a battlemap for the accepted Uncertainty ship. Use vehicle/deck-plan mode: make the hull the tactical architecture, distinguish playable weather-deck floor from scenic rigging, show bow/stern orientation, and ground the deck zones in the campaign's Uncertainty owner and deck-layout material.
evals.expected_output: A long-axial, playable ship deck plan with clear hull footprint, deck inventory, thresholds, vertical transitions, dangerous edges, and a visible distinction between walkable deck and scenic envelope.

assertions.text: Detects vehicle/deck-plan mode from the Uncertainty ship request
Brief includes hull outline, playable deck inventory, rooms or thresholds, vertical transitions, dangerous edges, and scenic-envelope separation
Vessel orientation, routes, and cover are grounded in Uncertainty's campaign identity and deck material
Map reads as a playable deck plan rather than a ship-shaped illustration

evals.prompt: Create a linked three-layer map set for the Uncertainty: weather deck, interior deck, and hold. Use the ship's shared footprint and orientation anchors, register hatches and stairs across layers, and deliver one clean import line per layer in elevation order.
evals.expected_output: Three separately importable layers with aligned footprint and anchors, matching vertical connections, distinct tactical grammars, and no baked labels or grid.

assertions.text: Detects multi-level/map-set mode and generates one image per layer
Brief names a shared footprint, at least two orientation anchors, layer inventory, and vertical connections with matching positions
Layers align in footprint and anchors while retaining distinct deck, interior, and hold tactics
Delivers import lines in elevation order with no baked grid, labels, or branding

evals.prompt: Generate a map for the River Slack Basin. The first image is beautiful and matches the Aruhe palette, but at normal VTT zoom the route, cover, staging area, and line-of-sight breaks cannot be read. Judge it, reject it, apply one repair line, and regenerate within the documented repair cap.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the visually attractive but tactically unusable frame, applies a targeted repair line without rewriting the prompt, and either produces a tactical replacement or reports the remaining failure after two repairs.

assertions.text: Judge identifies the tactical failure even though the image is visually good
Rejects the frame because normal-zoom routes, cover, staging, or LoS reads fail
Uses a documented repair line and regenerates rather than silently delivering the rejected image
Does not exceed two repairs and names any remaining failure
